Definition: Magbish, an Israelite, or a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Magbish is named once, in Ezra 2:30, where the children of Magbish, an hundred fifty and six, are counted among those who came back from the exile. Their hundred and fifty-six came home with the rest of the exiles, and their name is on the list.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a one-line headcount like this one still says the return was real: a hundred and fifty-six people came home.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
